name: Ahimaaz
bio:
Ahimaaz was the son of the priest Zadok. When David fled Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion and sent Zadok and Abiathar back into the city with the ark, he arranged for Ahimaaz and Abiathar's son Jonathan to stay behind with their fathers as runners, ready to carry word to David of anything David's spy Hushai learned inside Absalom's camp (2 Samuel 15:27-28, 36).

After Hushai's counsel defeated Ahithophel's, Ahimaaz and Jonathan waited at En Rogel, unable to risk being seen entering the city; a servant girl carried word to them to warn David not to delay crossing the Jordan. A boy spotted them and told Absalom, forcing the two to hide in a well at a house in Bahurim, which a woman covered and spread grain over to conceal them while Absalom's men searched and gave up. Once the danger passed, Ahimaaz and Jonathan hurried to David with the warning, and David's entire company crossed the Jordan by morning light, escaping just in time (2 Samuel 17:17-22). Later, during the climactic battle against Absalom's forces, Ahimaaz begged Joab to let him run and tell David the LORD had delivered him from his enemies, but Joab refused, sending Cushi instead since the news included Absalom's death; Ahimaaz pressed to run anyway and, by way of the plain, outran Cushi to reach David first, though he could not bring himself to tell the king plainly that Absalom was dead (2 Samuel 18:19-29).
